chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Bilal al-Muhallabi reported to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Rashid al-Isfahani narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: Ismail ibn Subayh informed us, saying: Salim ibn Abu Salim al-Misri narrated to us, from Abu Haroon al-Abdi, who said:

I held the opinion of the Khawarij, accepting no other opinion, until I sat with Abu Sa'id al-Khudri -- may Allah have mercy on him -- and heard him say: "People were ordered to do five things, and they performed four but left out one."

A man asked him: "O Abu Sa'id, what are the four things they performed?" He said: "The prayer, the zakat, the Hajj, and fasting during the month of Ramadan." He asked: "Then what is the one they left out?" He said: "The wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him."

The man said: "And is it indeed obligatory together with them?" Abu Sa'id said: "Yes, by the Lord of the Ka'bah!" The man said: "Then the people have indeed disbelieved!" Abu Sa'id said: "Then what is my fault?"

key_terms.الْخَوَارِج: An early Islamic sect that rebelled against both Ali and Mu'awiyah, known for extreme views on excommunication
key_terms.الْمُفْتَرَضَة: That which is made obligatory (fard) by God, indicating divine mandate
key_terms.وِلَايَة: Authority, guardianship, and divinely-appointed leadership, here referring to the obligation of allegiance to Ali ibn Abi Talib

ai.seo_question: What did Abu Sa'id al-Khudri say about the five obligations including the wilayah of Ali?
ai.summary: Abu Haroon al-Abdi, a former Kharijite, recounts how his views changed after hearing Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrate that people were commanded five obligations -- prayer, zakat, Hajj, fasting, and the wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib -- but they performed only four and abandoned the fifth. When asked if the wilayah was made obligatory alongside the other four, Abu Sa'id swore by the Lord of the Ka'bah that it was.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
